title: Enterprise, data, embedded & security patterns
literature: Fowler PoEAA (enterprise/data source/domain logic); POSA; embedded/real-time patterns (Douglass Real-Time Design Patterns; Pont); security patterns; each pattern realizes/refines a style.

members.name: Application Switching
members.what: Splits the system into independent executables of which only one runs at a time, each fitting the memory budget alone.

members.name: Authorization (security pattern)
members.what: A system-level structure defining which subjects may perform which actions on which protected resources, enforced at guarded access points.

members.name: Board Support Package
members.what: The packaging of all board-specific software - boot code, clock and pin configuration, device drivers, memory maps - into one named unit that adapts an OS or firmware stack to a particular hardware board.

members.name: Bounded Context
members.what: An explicit boundary within which a domain model and its ubiquitous language apply consistently; large systems are partitioned into several.

members.name: Chained Processors
members.what: Arranges multiple processors in a chain where a small always-on processor handles front-line work and wakes or feeds larger downstream processors only when needed.

members.name: Domain Model
members.what: Organizes domain logic as an interconnected object model where each object carries the data and behavior of one domain concept.

members.name: Dual-Core Lockstep
members.what: Two identical processor cores execute the same instruction stream cycle-aligned (one delayed a few cycles) while comparators check their outputs every cycle, signaling a fault on any divergence.

members.name: Five-Layer Architecture (RTDP)
members.what: A concrete whole-system layering template for real-time embedded applications (application, UI, communication, abstract OS, abstract hardware).

members.name: Functional Redundancy
members.what: Provide redundant components that are diversely designed and implemented but must produce the same output for the same input.

members.name: Half-Sync/Half-Async (system layering)
members.what: Layers a concurrent system into a synchronous service layer and an asynchronous event layer mediated by a queueing layer.

members.name: Hardware Abstraction Layer (architectural layer)
members.what: A dedicated layer in the firmware stack that presents hardware-independent interfaces for all peripheral and processor access, so every layer above it is portable across boards and silicon.

members.name: Health Monitor (ARINC 653)
members.what: A standardized architectural function that detects and reports faults at process, partition, and module level and applies configured recovery actions (restart, stop, switch) per level, defined by configuration tables rather than application

members.name: Hierarchical Control (RTDP)
members.what: Distributes control policy across a hierarchy in which upper controllers set goals/modes and lower controllers execute them locally.

members.name: MooN Voting Architecture
members.what: The safety-instrumented channel topologies named MooN in IEC 61508: N channels of which M must agree/demand for the safety function to act (1oo1, 1oo2, 2oo2, 2oo3, 1oo2D...), each with defined diagnostic and voting arrangements.

members.name: Master-Worker
members.what: A master component partitions work into independent tasks and dispatches them to a pool of identical worker components, then collects and combines their results.

members.name: Materialized View (architecture pattern)
members.what: Precomputed, query-shaped copies of data are generated and refreshed from source-of-truth stores to serve reads the source format handles poorly.

members.name: Model-View-Controller
members.what: Decomposes an interactive application into a model holding core data and logic, views presenting it, and controllers handling user input, with a change-propagation mechanism keeping them consistent.

members.name: Model-View-Intent
members.what: Structures the app as a reactive cycle: intents (user input streams) feed a model function producing state streams that the view renders.

members.name: Model-View-Presenter
members.what: UI structure where a presenter mediates all interaction between a (possibly passive) view and the model, absorbing presentation logic.

members.name: Model-View-ViewModel
members.what: UI structure where a view binds declaratively (data binding) to a view-model exposing view-shaped state and commands over the model.

members.name: Monitor-Actuator
members.what: A two-channel structure separating the actuation channel from an independent monitoring channel that checks the actuator's physical effect against setpoints and forces a fail-safe state on divergence.

members.name: Polyglot Persistence
members.what: A system deliberately uses multiple storage technologies, matching each data-management need to the store best suited for it.

members.name: Presentation Model
members.what: A self-contained class holding all view state and behavior, which the view synchronizes with; the toolkit-independent predecessor of MVVM.

members.name: Privilege Separation
members.what: Splits a program into a small privileged monitor process and unprivileged worker processes that request privileged operations over a narrow channel.

members.name: Recursive Containment (RTDP)
members.what: Decomposes the system recursively into parts that are themselves structured like systems, to any needed depth.

members.name: Recursive Control
members.what: Structures a real-time control system as a recursive hierarchy in which every component pairs its functional part with a control part, uniformly at all levels.

members.name: Replication
members.what: Provide multiple identical copies of a component so their results can be voted on or a copy can take over; effective against random hardware faults.

members.name: Reporting Database
members.what: A separate database, fed from the operational store, structured and indexed for reporting/analytics queries.

members.name: Safety Executive
members.what: A centralized component that tracks safety-relevant events and coordinates all shutdown, recovery, and fail-safe transitions for the system, separating safety policy from the functional channels it supervises.

members.name: Sandbox
members.what: Isolate an instance of the system from the real world so it can be experimented on without permanent consequences, including virtualizing uncontrollable resources (system clock, memory, battery, network); stubs, mocks, and dependency inject

members.name: Self-Contained Component
members.what: Organizes code into components each owning its directory, exposing one header interface, with dependencies pointing only toward more fundamental components.

members.name: Service Layer
members.what: A layer of application services defines the system's available operations, coordinating domain logic, transactions and responses per operation.

members.name: Single Sign-On
members.what: One authentication event with a trusted authority yields tokens/tickets accepted by many independent systems.

members.name: Someone in Charge
members.what: For every fault-tolerance activity some identified component is in charge of seeing it through to completion.

members.name: Strangler Fig
members.what: Incrementally build the new system around the edges of the old, intercepting and redirecting functionality until the legacy system is fully displaced.

members.name: Supervision Tree (OTP)
members.what: Workers are organized under a tree of supervisors whose only job is to monitor children and apply restart strategies (one-for-one, one-for-all, rest-for-one).

members.name: Table Module
members.what: Organizes domain logic with one class per database table, each instance handling all rows of its table.

members.name: The Elm Architecture
members.what: App structured as an immutable model, a pure update function folding messages into the model, and a pure view function rendering it.

members.name: Time and Space Partitioning
members.what: An operating-system-enforced structure in which applications run in partitions with statically allocated memory regions (space) and fixed cyclic execution windows (time), so no partition can affect another's resources or timing.

members.name: Transaction Script
members.what: Organizes all domain logic as one procedure per business transaction, each handling its request from presentation to database.

members.name: Triple Modular Redundancy
members.what: Three identical channels compute in parallel and a voter forwards the majority result, masking any single channel failure without interruption of service.

members.name: Trusted Execution Environment
members.what: A hardware-isolated execution partition runs security-critical code and holds secrets, exposing only a narrow call interface to the untrusted rich OS beside it.

members.name: Units of Mitigation
members.what: Divides the system into the units within which errors are contained and recovery is performed - the granularity of restart and repair.
